I'm working on a bug in the Ghost Admin email settings UI.

*   When a color picker is opened inside the EmailDesignModal (e.g. via ButtonColorField), pressing the Escape key must close only the color picker and must NOT call the modal's onClose callback or remove the modal from the DOM.

*   This Escape key interception must work both when the color picker popover content has fully mounted AND when Escape is pressed immediately after opening the color picker (before the popover content has finished rendering/mounting).

*   The EmailDesignModal must remain visible in the DOM (identifiable by its testId) after Escape is pressed while a color picker is open or in the process of opening.

*   The ButtonColorField component must render a clickable element labeled 'Button color' that, when clicked, opens a color picker popover.

*   The EmailDesignProvider must accept accentColor (string), settings (EmailDesign), and onSettingsChange (function) props and provide context to child components including EmailDesignModal and ButtonColorField.

*   DEFAULT_EMAIL_DESIGN must be exported from the types module as the default email design settings object compatible with EmailDesignProvider's settings prop.


*   Interface details: Type: Component
Name: EmailDesignModal
Location: apps/admin-x-settings/src/components/settings/email-design/email-design-modal.tsx
Description: A modal component for customizing email design settings. Accepts props: open (boolean), preview (ReactNode), sidebar (ReactNode), testId (string), title (string), onClose (function), onSave (function). The modal should remain open when Escape is pressed while a color picker within the sidebar is open.

Type: Component

Description: A design field component that renders a "Button color" label and opens a color picker popover when clicked. When the color picker is open (or in the process of opening), pressing Escape should close only the color picker — it must NOT propagate the Escape key event in a way that closes the parent EmailDesignModal.

Type: Component

Description: A context provider for email design state. Accepts props: accentColor (string), settings (EmailDesign), onSettingsChange (function). Wraps EmailDesignModal and its field components.

I now understand the bug. Radix's `useEscapeKeydown` attaches capture-phase listeners on `document`, and each `DismissableLayer` only reacts if it's the highest layer. When the popover content is mounted, it's the highest layer so the modal correctly ignores Escape. But when Escape is pressed *before* the popover content (its `DismissableLayer`) has mounted, the Dialog is still the highest layer and its `onEscapeKeyDown` fires → `handleClose()` → modal closes. That's the bug.

The robust fix is a self-contained handler in `ColorPickerField` that intercepts Escape on `window` in the capture phase (which runs *before* Radix's `document` listeners), closes only the picker, and stops the event from reaching the Dialog — working regardless of whether the popover content has mounted.

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I did.

## Root cause

Ghost's `EmailDesignModal` (a Radix `Dialog`) and the color picker (a Radix `Popover`) both rely on `@radix-ui/react-dismissable-layer`, which registers Escape handlers on `document` in the capture phase. A layer only dismisses when it's the *top-most* layer. 

- **When the popover content is mounted**, the popover is the top layer, so the Dialog correctly ignores Escape. ✅
- **When Escape is pressed immediately after opening** (before the popover's `DismissableLayer` has mounted), the Dialog is still the top-most layer, so its `onEscapeKeyDown` → `handleClose()` fires and the modal closes. ❌ ← the bug.

## Fix

Everything the task describes already existed except the fix for the pre-mount case (`EmailDesignProvider`, `EmailDesignModal`, `ButtonColorField`, `DEFAULT_EMAIL_DESIGN` were all present and matched the required API).

I added a single self-contained handler in `color-picker-field.tsx` (`apps/admin-x-settings/src/components/settings/email-design/color-picker-field.tsx`) — the shared component behind `ButtonColorField` and every other color field:

- While the picker is `open`, it listens for `keydown` on `window` in the **capture phase**. Since `window` precedes `document` in the capture phase, this runs *ahead of* every Radix `document`-level Escape handler.
- On Escape it calls `stopImmediatePropagation()` + `preventDefault()` so the event never reaches the Dialog (modal can't close, `onClose` never fires), then `setOpen(false)` to close only the picker.
- The listener is keyed to `ColorPickerField`'s own `open` state, which flips synchronously on click — so it's attached **regardless of whether the popover content has finished mounting**, covering both required scenarios.

## Verification
- All 16 existing `test/unit/email-design/` tests pass; no test files were modified.
- ESLint and TypeScript are clean on the changed file.
- A throwaway integration test (rendering the real modal + provider + `ButtonColorField`, then pressing Escape) confirmed the modal stays in the DOM and `onClose` isn't called for both the mounted and immediate cases; I removed it after confirming, per the instruction not to touch the test dir.

Placing the fix in `ColorPickerField` (rather than `ButtonColorField` or the modal) means all color fields inherit the correct behavior consistently.
